title.narrative: SSD020N South Sudan JR 2024-2026

description.promeva:title: Description (English)
description.narrative:
Protection activities will be implemented in 7 locations (CARE in PIBOR) and aligned with other funding in the 8th location (Akobo County). SSJR partners will reach 294,823 people. The activities include protection prevention measures, child protection, information sharing, capacity strengthening, support to child soldiers/ separated/ unaccompanied children, GBV prevention and response, tracing and reunification. Some of the lessons learnt by the SSJR protection partners that will be incorporated in the design for 2024-2026 are: - advocacy strategies should be child-led and community driven; - adolescent sexual reproductive health should be integrated into child protection/MHPSS concerns; - the engagement of men and boys is integral to the success of GBV outcomes; - the importance of awareness in challenging norms and other cultural practices; - encouraging more resilient programming to enable community explore more self/community reliant approach; - complimenting GBV programs with economic empowerment initiatives for women and girls. The protection partners will adhere to the MHPSS global guidelines, child protection minimum standards, child protection area of responsibility case management guidelines and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Data Management/protection protocols, IASC Gender with Age Marker, the Washington Group Questions, IASC guidelines for disability inclusion in humanitarian action, the Ministry of Health guidelines on disability inclusion.
CARE
GBV Activities:
•Refurbishment and equipping of safe spaces for women and girls at risk of GBV for increased access to quality specialized GBV services (support to 3 WGFS)
•Provision of GBV quality case management
•PSS Activities
•Contextually relevant skills-building for GBV survivors
•Provision of dignity kits for GBV survivors
•GBV and peace building community outreach (IEC material)
•Conduct safety audit and update the GBV referral pathways
•GBV phone and hotline
•Establish peace committees and peace clubs to carryout reconciliation and peace building activities.
•Establish Engagement of Men and Boys (EMB) groups and conduct EMB community sessions
•Advocacy products
Result areas:
1. People in need are reached by the implementation of specific GBV prevention measures
2. GBV survivors receive appropriate responses
3. Protection advocacy products are produced and disseminated, and protection advocacy meetings/events are held
4. Capacity building aimed at increased knowledge on the protection issues
5. An increase in persons with increased/appropriate information on relevant rights and/or entitlements
6. Protection information disseminated for target populations to receive appropriate responses for the prevention and response to violence

The influx of 3,925 IDPs due to flooding from Aug 2025 increased this activity’s caseload. The IDPs needed to be onboarded so that they get to understand their rights, and access necessary support services, including health, legal, and psychosocial assistance and other protection information during their reintegration process.
CARE established 6 groups of EMBs in the three locations of Verteth, Akilo and Gumuruk Payam. Each group comprised on 30 individuals, equally divided into boys and men. The EMB approach engages male (men and boys) to challenge gender inequality to shift beliefs, behaviors and practices at household and community levels in support of gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls. Some of the topics covered included gender and power, sexuality, fatherhood, violence, making change, taking action among others. During the EMB sessions, men and boys have been encouraged to abandon harmful stereotypes that discriminate against women and embrace respectful, healthy relationships. They were also encouraged to support the human rights of all people in their community. The EMB approach recognizes that men and boys are key actors in gender transformation and can be obstacles or allies for gender equality. Thus, by engaging men and boys, it reduces the barriers women and girls face in building their own individual agency, address inequitable power relations, and ensures changes in power dynamics and social structures that are sustained. 1. Community meetings which were a vital strategy in preventing, reporting, and responding to child recruitment in Rubkona County, South Sudan, across individual, community, and national levels. These are how these meetings effectively contribute to each level: • At Individual Level, UNIDOR has been conducting community meetings that served as a platform to educate parents, guardians, and children about the dangers and illegality of child recruitment. They inform individuals about the physical and psychological harm involved, as well as the long-term consequences for children. Secondly, these meetings offered support to families at risk, equipping them with information on how to protect their children from recruiters. They also provided resources (cash) and contacts for reporting any attempts or incidents of child recruitment. • At community Level, the community meetings emphasized the collective responsibility of the community to protect children, which fostered a sense of communal duty as UNIDRO encouraged community members to look out for one another’s children and report suspicious activities. These meetings also strengthened local networks and created a support system where information could quickly get disseminated, and responses were coordinated. Thus, it helped in identifying and supporting vulnerable families.

comment.narrative: CARE activated a Crisis Modifier through partner UNIDOR (incident date 12 May 2026; 3-month response, June–August 2026), committing $50,000 (€44,473) to scale up lifesaving nutrition services through mobile/outreach OTP and TSFP sites in Yornhail, Chamzaar, and Norlamwel payams. The response targets 600 pregnant and lactating women and 1,000 children aged 6–59 months (15% with disabilities), including treatment of 300 SAM and 900 MAM children, screening and treatment of 600 PLW, MIYCN counselling, three kitchen gardens, hygiene promotion, and training of 500 caregivers on the Family MUAC approach complementing UNIDOR's ongoing SSJR nutrition programming in Rubkona.

In July 2024, through the AAP system and engagement with local actors under GPAA, JR partners reported a catastrophic situation in Lekuangole where 11 people died due to starvation. Based on these reports and findings from the Initial Rapid Needs Assessment, CARE implemented adaptive programming by providing cash for protection to 224 households (F=113, M=111), including widowers (50), persons with special needs (55), persons with disabilities (18), orphans (22), deaf individuals (6), elderly persons (59), and blind individuals (14). In addition, through the crisis modifier and following community consultations for flood response, one key adaptation was the construction of dikes in Panyijiar County, Unity State. These dikes, constructed by UNIDOR, significantly contributed to reducing flood impacts in the affected communities.
